title: CASE M-10Q — the machine
intro: Field Recovery reopened the file on an instrument that needed no map, no clerk and no signature: a tool that got a sum wrong, and a sum that decided who kept a house. In 2018 a bank said, in a quarterly filing to the SEC, that an automated underwriting tool had been reading the numbers wrong for years — and that the wrong number had been the difference between a modification and a foreclosure. No one drew a line this time. Nothing was stamped. A figure came out of a machine, and the figure was the house. Four instruments. Three live in the public record. The fourth you have to hear for yourself, in the deep stacks, where a radio reads a list one line at a time and does not stop until it reaches yours.

stations.title: i · the word
stations.clue: In August 2018 the bank's quarterly filing — the 10-Q — disclosed what an automated mortgage-modification underwriting tool had been doing. The headlines called it a software error. The filing's own name for it is narrower, and the reporters set it in quotation marks: two words, the second of them 'error'. Open the report, find the quoted phrase, and file its first word. HousingWire quotes the phrase directly; the filing itself is on SEC EDGAR. The System never says 'mistake'. It says exactly this.
stations.prompt: the first word of the filing's quoted two-word name for the error — one word
stations.onSolve: not a decision. not a policy. not a person. a sum, done wrong, by a tool that could not know it was wrong. the clerk did not lie — it has no field for that. now count what the sum cost.

stations.title: ii · the count
stations.clue: The same filing put a number on it. Loans already in foreclosure between the thirteenth of April 2010 and the twentieth of October 2015 were run through the tool, and the tool said no — or said nothing at all — to customers who should have been offered a modification. About how many? The filing rounds it, and every report repeats the rounded figure. CNBC carried it on the seventh of August; HousingWire carried it too. File the figure exactly as the record gives it, nothing else around it.

link.label: CNBC, 7 August 2018 — the error, by the numbers (free)

stations.prompt: about how many customers the tool wrongly denied, or never offered, a modification — digits only
stations.onSolve: that was the first count. of those, roughly four hundred lost the house — a figure with a roof on it. the tool was not finished, though. it had one more thing to do, and it did it in november: it counted again.

stations.title: iii · the recount
stations.clue: In November 2018 the bank filed its next 10-Q and corrected itself. The review had widened, and the count of affected customers rose. HousingWire reported the new figure in November 2018; the filing rounds it, as before. The primary is the bank's third-quarter 2018 10-Q on SEC EDGAR; the free HousingWire report carries the same figure. File the revised count. Not the old one, not the difference — the number the machine settled on the second time.
stations.prompt: the revised count of affected customers, as the november filing gave it — digits only
stations.onSolve: the clerk recounted and the number grew. that is the whole method: a figure, and later a bigger figure, and never once a name. one instrument left, and it is not in any filing. it is in the deep stacks, and it counts too.

stations.title: iv · the radio
stations.clue: The last instrument you have to hear. Go down past the habitable zone into the deep stacks — level 2, pipe dreams, or level 3, electrical station. Carry a radio (the vending machines stock it) and switch it on down there. Near the surface the radio only crackles to life and says nothing; in the deep stacks it reads a list aloud, one number group at a time, slow and patient, not talking to you. Switch it off and on again and it reads the next group. Listen through the whole cycle — the tally in brackets on the screen will confirm you — and count how many groups it reads before it stops. It will tell you, when it gets there, whose the last one was.

stations.prompt: how many number groups the station reads before it stops — digits only
stations.onSolve: it reads the last group, then stops. that one was yours. the machine upstairs counted, then counted again, and never said a name. this one does not say a name either. it just keeps reading until it reaches your line.

reward.title: the machine is read.
reward.text: Four instruments and not one signature. A tool got a sum wrong; the wrong sum decided who kept a house; a count came out, and later a bigger count, and the file never once needed a name to do it. That is the System as Field Recovery keeps meeting it — not cruel, not careful, a clerk with no face, running the arithmetic until it reaches your line. A calculation. A count. A house. A thing can lose its place and keep its name, and the ledger will not notice either way. Down in the deep stacks a radio reads the same kind of list, patient, one group at a time, with your line last. The record calls that the arithmetic. Go and read where the count is going.
reward.linkLabel: ▸ the arithmetic — where the count is going
